=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- workflow-templates/ai-check-failure-triage.yml | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The last-run replaces `github.event.workflow_run.path` (which exposes the run's path, including an optional `@refs/heads/...` suffix) with `github.event.workflow.path`, which is not part of the `workflow_run` Actions context.
  WHY: With `null != null` evaluating to `false`, the new `if` predicate is always false and the triage job is skipped for every `workflow_run` event. The wrapper would never dispatch triage on PR runs, regressing the workflow that the last-run README/changelog fragment claim to fix. The unit-test fixture was extended with a synthetic top-level `workflow` object so it passes against the mock payload, but the mock no longer matches the real GitHub Actions payload for `workflow_run`, hiding the regression from the test suite.
- scripts/clarify_isolated_run.sh: `source_root="${CLARIFY_SOURCE_ROOT:-${PWD}}"; if [ ! -d "${source_root}" ] || [ -L "${source_root}" ]; then echo '::error::Clarify source root unavailable' >&2; exit 1; fi` | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The script rejects every symlinked source root via `[ -L "${source_root}" ]` before the subsequent `cd "${source_root}" && pwd -P` canonicalization.
  WHY: Local-dev / non-runner invocations of the helper exit early with `exit 1` and never reach Docker. CI callers (`check_failure_triage.sh`) are unaffected because they pass `CLARIFY_SOURCE_ROOT="${SOURCE_ROOT}"` (a non-symlinked path), but the documented `CLARIFY_SOURCE_ROOT: $PWD` default becomes a footgun. The `pwd -P` canonicalization on the next line already neutralizes symlink-based path confusion, so the explicit `-L` rejection is redundant for non-malicious callers and only blocks them.
- tests/test_ci_failure_workflow_run_triggers.py: `_run_event(...) adds "workflow": {"path": path.split("@", 1)[0]} next to workflow_run; _evaluate(condition, "workflow_run", _run_event("Any name", path=f"{own}@refs/heads/main")) asserts the suffixed path is still excluded.` | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The fixture builds an event payload that does not match what GitHub Actions actually delivers for `workflow_run`.
  WHY: By adding a top-level `workflow` object the test author makes the new condition evaluate to the expected value, but the real workflow reads `github.event.workflow.path` against a payload where that field is absent. A CI run of this test passes locally yet the workflow change still regresses in production because the simulated event payload diverges from the real `workflow_run` Actions context. Operators relying on the green test will ship a broken predicate.
